title: EPILEPSY, FAMILIAL ADULT MYOCLONIC, 2
alt_titles: CORTICAL MYOCLONIC TREMOR WITH EPILEPSY, FAMILIAL, 2
CORTICAL MYOCLONUS AND EPILEPSY, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-2 (FAME2) is caused by expansion of an intronic pentanucleotide (ATTTC) repeat in the STARD7 gene (616712) on chromosome 2q11.2.

checks.claim: Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-2 (FAME2) is caused by expansion of an intronic pentanucleotide (ATTTC) repeat in the STARD7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we provide evidence that chr2-linked FAME (FAME2) is caused by an expansion of an ATTTC pentamer within the first intron of STARD7.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: The STARD7 gene is located on chromosome 2q11.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Most families link to chromosomes 8q24 or 2p11.2-q11.2
checks.explanation: The paper places STARD7 on chr2 within the FAME2 interval. Giving the band as 2q11.2 is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-2 (FAME2) is an autosomal dominant disorder. Guerrini et al. (2001) described its main features as predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus and rare seizures, with generalized tonic-clonic seizures in all patients. Onset was between ages 12 and 50 years, which covers adolescence and adulthood. Electrophysiologic findings included high-amplitude (giant) somatosensory evoked potentials and an enhanced C reflex at rest (Guerrini et al., 2001), and Striano et al. (2005) confirmed cortical reflex myoclonus. Labauge et al. (2002) found a premyoclonus spike on jerk-locked EEG averaging and described a nonprogressive, generally benign course with infrequent seizures.

checks.claim: Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-2 (FAME2) is an autosomal dominant disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance was autosomal dominant with high penetrance.
checks.explanation: The paper calls the disorder ADCME. Treating it as the draft's FAME2 relies on other sources.

checks.claim: The main features of FAME2 include predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus.
checks.evidence_quote: It was characterized by predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus (all patients)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: FAME2 is characterized by rare seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: Most individuals had rarely suffered seizures and had a normal cognitive level, but three individuals with intractable seizures had mild mental retardation.
checks.explanation: Most patients had rare seizures, though three had intractable seizures.

checks.claim: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures occurred in all FAME2 patients described by Guerrini et al. (2001).
checks.evidence_quote: generalized tonic-clonic seizures (all patients)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Onset of FAME2 was between ages 12 and 50 years, covering adolescence and adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: eight individuals presented with a non-progressive disorder with onset between the ages of 12 and 50 years
checks.explanation: The age range matches. 'Adolescence and adulthood' is the draft's reasonable reading of that range.

checks.claim: FAME2 patients had high-amplitude (giant) somatosensory evoked potentials.
checks.evidence_quote: somatosensory and visual evoked potentials were of high amplitude
checks.explanation: The paper says 'high amplitude'. The draft's 'giant' is a gloss on that.

checks.claim: FAME2 patients had an enhanced C reflex at rest.
checks.evidence_quote: The C-reflex at rest was enhanced
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Striano et al. (2005) confirmed cortical reflex myoclonus in FAME2.
checks.evidence_quote: Electrophysiological study confirmed the presence of cortical reflex myoclonus in all affected members.
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms cortical reflex myoclonus in a family linked to chromosome 2p, which is the FAME2 locus. This matches the claim.

checks.claim: Labauge et al. (2002) found a premyoclonus spike on jerk-locked EEG averaging.
checks.evidence_quote: premyoclonus spike detected by means of the jerk-locked averaging EEG method
checks.explanation: The premyoclonus spike appears in the background definition of FAME, not as a result in this family. The results only say electrophysiologic studies confirmed FAME in five patients. Only the abstract was supplied, so any specific jerk-locked averaging findings would be in the full text and can't be checked.

checks.claim: Labauge et al. (2002) described a nonprogressive, generally benign course with infrequent seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: infrequent epileptic seizures, nonprogressive course
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the nonprogressive course and infrequent seizures as defining features of FAME (background), not as observations described in this family. The abstract does not say "generally benign".

paragraphs.text: Guerrini et al. (2001) described a family with an autosomal dominant disorder that they called autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME). Onset was between ages 12 and 50 years. All patients had predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Some patients also had complex partial (focal) seizures. A neurophysiologic study of the myoclonus suggested a cortical origin.

checks.claim: Guerrini et al. (2001) described a family with an autosomal dominant disorder they called autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME).
checks.evidence_quote: We defined this disorder as autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME).
checks.explanation: The paper describes a single pedigree with autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Onset of ADCME in the family described by Guerrini et al. (2001) was between ages 12 and 50 years.
checks.evidence_quote: onset between the ages of 12 and 50 years
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: All ADCME patients described by Guerrini et al. (2001) had predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus.
checks.evidence_quote: predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus (all patients)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: All ADCME patients described by Guerrini et al. (2001) had generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: generalized tonic-clonic seizures (all patients)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Some ADCME patients described by Guerrini et al. (2001) also had complex partial (focal) seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: complex partial seizures (three patients)
checks.explanation: Three patients had complex partial seizures.

checks.claim: A neurophysiologic study of the myoclonus in the ADCME family suggested a cortical origin.
checks.evidence_quote: A neurophysiological study of the myoclonus suggested a cortical origin.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Guerrini et al. (2001) reported autosomal dominant inheritance with high penetrance in the family they described.

checks.claim: Guerrini et al. (2001) reported autosomal dominant inheritance in the ADCME family they described.
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance was autosomal dominant with high penetrance.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Guerrini et al. (2001) reported high penetrance in the ADCME family they described.
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance was autosomal dominant with high penetrance.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: In the family with ADCME, Guerrini et al. (2001) found linkage to the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2, at 2p11.1-q12.2.

checks.claim: Guerrini et al. (2001) found linkage of ADCME in the family to the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2, at 2p11.1-q12.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Genome-wide linkage analysis identified a critical region spanning 12.4 cM between markers D2S2161 and D2S1897 in 2p11.1-q12.2
checks.explanation: The paper also says the gene maps to 'the centromeric region of chromosome 2', which matches 'pericentromeric'.

paragraphs.text: De Falco et al. (2003) studied 2 Italian families with benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME) and found linkage to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2. This locus was distinct from the BAFME locus previously mapped to chromosome 8q24 (FAME1). The authors suggested that BAFME in these families might be allelic with ADCME.

checks.claim: De Falco et al. (2003) studied 2 Italian families with benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME).
checks.evidence_quote: The authors report a clinical and electrophysiologic study of two Italian BAFME families
checks.explanation: Abstract states two Italian BAFME families were studied.

checks.claim: De Falco et al. (2003) found linkage of BAFME in 2 Italian families to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2.
checks.evidence_quote: two Italian BAFME families showing linkage to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2
checks.explanation: Linkage interval matches exactly.

checks.claim: The chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 BAFME locus was distinct from the BAFME locus previously mapped to chromosome 8q24 (FAME1).
checks.evidence_quote: Benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME) has been mapped to chromosome 8q24; however, genetic heterogeneity has been recently suggested.
checks.explanation: Abstract cites prior 8q24 mapping and genetic heterogeneity, and reports a new chromosome 2 locus, so the loci are distinct. Calling the 8q24 locus FAME1 is standard naming.

checks.claim: De Falco et al. (2003) suggested that BAFME in the 2 Italian families might be allelic with ADCME.
checks.evidence_quote: suggests a possible allelism with the recently described autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy syndrome
checks.explanation: ADCME stands for autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; the abstract suggests possible allelism.

paragraphs.text: Madia et al. (2008) studied 5 Italian families with BAFME linked to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2. A shared haplotype segregated with the disease in all families, indicating that the same mutation had been inherited from a common ancestor (a founder effect).

checks.claim: Madia et al. (2008) studied 5 Italian families with BAFME linked to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Significant linkage was found on chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 and a maximum cumulative lod score of 18.5 was found for markers D2S2161 and D2S388.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes five Italian BAFME families that show significant linkage to 2p11.1-q12.2.

checks.claim: A shared haplotype segregated with BAFME in all 5 Italian families studied by Madia et al. (2008).
checks.evidence_quote: The haplotype "5332" of adjacent markers D2S388, D2S2216, D2S113, and D2S2175 segregates with the disease in all families
checks.explanation: The abstract says the shared haplotype segregates with the disease in all five families.

checks.claim: The shared haplotype in the 5 Italian BAFME families indicated a founder effect, with the same mutation inherited from a common ancestor.
checks.evidence_quote: segregates with the disease in all families indicating that the same mutation inherited from a common ancestor segregates in these families.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly, and the title calls it a founder haplotype.

paragraphs.text: Labauge et al. (2002) excluded linkage of a family to the familial adult myoclonic epilepsy/BAFME locus, which established that the disorder is genetically heterogeneous. De Fusco et al. (2014) noted that other families with similar forms of epilepsy had been linked to chromosomes 8q, 5p, and 3q. Corbett et al. (2019) noted that intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions in different genes had been reported at several of these loci.

checks.claim: Labauge et al. (2002) excluded linkage of a family to the familial adult myoclonic epilepsy/BAFME locus.
checks.evidence_quote: Exclusion of linkage of this family to the locus for familial adult myoclonic epilepsy/benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy established the genetic heterogeneity of this disorder.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The exclusion of linkage by Labauge et al. (2002) established that familial adult myoclonic epilepsy is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Exclusion of linkage of this family to the locus for familial adult myoclonic epilepsy/benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy established the genetic heterogeneity of this disorder.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: De Fusco et al. (2014) noted that other families with similar forms of epilepsy had been linked to chromosomes 8q, 5p, and 3q.
checks.evidence_quote: Additional pedigrees affected by similar forms of epilepsy have been associated with chromosomes 8q, 5p, and 3q, but none of the causing genes has been identified.
checks.explanation: The abstract says outright that other pedigrees with similar forms of epilepsy were linked to 8q, 5p and 3q.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) noted that intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions in different genes had been reported at several familial adult myoclonic epilepsy loci.
checks.evidence_quote: replicating the findings in the cases of FAME with expansions in SAMD12, TNRC6A, RAPGEF2,, and the report of a similar expansion in MARCH6 causing chr5-linked FAME.
checks.explanation: The paper describes similar intronic repeat expansions in other genes, including at the chr8 (SAMD12) and chr5 (MARCH6) FAME loci.

paragraphs.text: Corbett et al. (2019) studied families with chromosome 2-linked FAME (FAME2). In affected members they identified an expansion of an ATTTC pentanucleotide repeat in the first intron of the STARD7 gene. The ATTTC insertion was accompanied by expansion of the endogenous ATTTT (AAAAT on the forward strand) repeat. The ATTTC expansion segregated with the disorder and was not found in controls. The endogenous intron 1 repeat varied in length in the normal population but was not expanded to the same extent as in individuals with FAME. STARD7 transcript expression did not differ significantly. Corbett et al. (2019) noted that similar ATTTC expansions had been implicated at other FAME loci. They suggested that the repeat sequence alone is pathogenic, independent of any effect on the gene in which it lies.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) studied families with chromosome 2-linked FAME (FAME2).
checks.evidence_quote: we provide evidence that chr2-linked FAME (FAME2) is caused by an expansion of an ATTTC pentamer within the first intron of STARD7.
checks.explanation: The study focuses on chr2-linked FAME families.

checks.claim: In affected members of FAME2 families, Corbett et al. (2019) identified an expansion of an ATTTC pentanucleotide repeat in the first intron of the STARD7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We screen for an intronic ATTTC expansion in the first intron of STARD7 by repeat-primed PCR and show it segregates with FAME2 in 158 affected individuals from 22 families.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The ATTTC insertion in STARD7 intron 1 was accompanied by expansion of the endogenous ATTTT (AAAAT on the forward strand) repeat.
checks.evidence_quote: The pathogenic ATTTC insertion and expansion was always accompanied by the endogenous ATTTT pentanucleotide repeat in all cases of FAME2 that we describe here
checks.explanation: The forward-strand AAAAT notation and the expansion of the ATTTT repeat are also described in the Results ("expansion of an ATTTT repeat and insertion of an ATTTC repeat").

checks.claim: The STARD7 ATTTC expansion segregated with FAME2 in the families.
checks.evidence_quote: The ATTTC expansions segregate in 158/158 individuals typically affected by FAME from 22 pedigrees
checks.explanation: Segregation is stated directly.

checks.claim: The STARD7 ATTTC expansion was not found in controls.
checks.evidence_quote: The ATTTC repeat expansion did not amplify in any of 28 control DNA samples extracted from unaffected individuals unrelated to FAME.
checks.explanation: The repeat was also absent from WGS data of 69 controls.

checks.claim: The endogenous STARD7 intron 1 repeat varied in length in the normal population.
checks.evidence_quote: The endogenous ATTTT repeat in intron 1 of STARD7 was also found to be variable in length in the normal population but not expanded to the same extent as repeats found in individuals with FAME.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The endogenous STARD7 intron 1 repeat in the normal population was not expanded to the same extent as in individuals with FAME.
checks.evidence_quote: The endogenous ATTTT repeat in intron 1 of STARD7 was also found to be variable in length in the normal population but not expanded to the same extent as repeats found in individuals with FAME.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: STARD7 transcript expression did not differ significantly in individuals with the FAME2 repeat expansion.
checks.evidence_quote: showed no significant differences in STARD7 transcript expression in patient-derived fibroblast cell lines
checks.explanation: RT-qPCR and RNA-Seq both showed no significant difference. The draft leaves out that this was measured in fibroblasts, but the claim is consistent with the paper.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) noted that similar ATTTC expansions had been implicated at other FAME loci.
checks.evidence_quote: These data, in combination with other genes bearing similar mutations that have been implicated in FAME, suggest ATTTC expansions may cause this disorder, irrespective of the genomic locus involved.
checks.explanation: Stated in the abstract and discussion.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) suggested that the ATTTC repeat sequence alone is pathogenic, independent of any effect on the gene in which it lies.
checks.evidence_quote: These data suggest the repeat sequence alone is pathogenic, independent of an effect on the coding sequence of the encompassing gene.
checks.explanation: The draft says "any effect on the gene" where the paper says "the coding sequence of the encompassing gene". Expression was also unaffected, so the meaning is close enough.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus of cortical origin
Focal (complex partial) seizures in some patients
